subject: Biology
title: T Cells: The Commanders
description: Learn T Cells: The Commanders in one minute.

hook.text: T cells are trained in the thymus gland. Those that attack your own body are destroyed before graduation.

buildup.text: Helper T cells coordinate the immune response. Killer T cells destroy infected cells directly.

discovery.text: Each T cell recognizes one specific antigen—a molecular shape on a pathogen's surface.

twist.text: HIV attacks helper T cells specifically, collapsing the immune system's command structure.

climax.text: Without T cells, even harmless infections become lethal—which is why AIDS is so devastating.

punchline.text: Kill the commander, and the army falls apart.

details.summary: T cells are lymphocytes that orchestrate and execute adaptive immune responses. Helper T cells coordinate immune attacks by activating B cells and macrophages, cytotoxic T cells directly kill infected or cancerous cells, and regulatory T cells prevent autoimmune overreaction.
details.whyItMatters: T cells are the commanders of adaptive immunity. HIV's devastation comes from destroying helper T cells, and cancer immunotherapy works by unleashing cytotoxic T cells against tumors.
takeaways: Helper T cells coordinate immune responses by activating other immune cells
Cytotoxic T cells directly kill virus-infected and cancerous cells
Regulatory T cells prevent autoimmune attacks on the body's own tissues

faq.question: Why are helper T cells so important to the immune system?
faq.answer: Helper T cells are the coordinators that activate B cells to produce antibodies, boost macrophage killing ability, and help cytotoxic T cells mature. Without them, the adaptive immune system cannot mount effective responses. This is exactly why HIV, which destroys them, is so devastating.

faq.question: How do cytotoxic T cells kill infected cells?
faq.answer: Cytotoxic T cells recognize viral antigens displayed on infected cell surfaces via MHC class I molecules. They attach and release perforin, which punches holes in the target membrane, and granzymes, which enter through the holes and trigger programmed cell death.
